mission: Each character processes the Codex differently — the four positions deepen. Torin's rationalization begins in earnest: if the lattice is imposed, the technique isn't violation but correction.
why_now: The Codex has provided intellectual ammunition for all positions — the group must process before the next crisis
conflict: Torin's interpretation of the Codex is seductive and logically sound. Sera counters with experience — she's felt de-structuring and knows what it costs. Kael observes that both sides prove his point: conviction is a trap.
turning_point: Torin makes an argument so elegant that Ben catches himself agreeing before he pulls back. The technique's danger isn't that it's obviously wrong — it's that it's intellectually beautiful.
opening_hook: Torin holds the Codex fragment and doesn't flinch. Everyone else did.
closing_hook: Sera, very quietly to Ben: 'I have heard that argument before. From a man I followed into a war.' She doesn't say Gavran's name. She doesn't need to.
emotional_trajectory: Intellectual engagement -> seductive logic -> Sera's cold water

stakes.personal: Ben nearly seduced by Torin's interpretation — a warning about his own susceptibility
stakes.interpersonal: Sera beginning to trust Ben enough to warn him privately
stakes.external: Torin's relationship with the technique is deepening, not weakening

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — common area, then private corridor exchange
sensory_details: Torin's Force presence when he holds the Codex — the heaviness lifting, something lighter and more dangerous replacing it; Sera's jaw tight; Kael's expression: 'I told you so' without saying it
notes: Torin's arc: lie_reinforced — each intellectual justification strengthens his conviction. Sera's arc: lie_reinforced — her rigid certainty feels validated by Torin's drift. She's right about the danger but rigid about the response.
